clue.text: In keeping ammunition at a Catholic house, lapse is universal and very bad (7 23,supposedly)

definitions.note: the line the castaway named in the linked entry is said to have spoken, a phrase rather than a noun

indicators.note: one piece keeping another holds it inside, so the first word wraps round the next

parts.note: taken as written
AMMO is the everyday short form of ammunition
RC stands for Roman Catholic
a lapse or moral failing is a fall, as in the Fall of Man
taken as written
U is the film-certificate letter for a universal rating

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoilt, so the word very is reworked into new order

explanation.surface: Someone hoarding ammunition in a Catholic house has fallen into a universal and very bad sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 7 23 is the Juan Fernandez castaway, and this is the opening line of William Cowper's poem in his voice, hence 'supposedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper's poem on the marooned sailor opens with this boast, so the castaway supposedly declared himself ruler of his island.

clue.text: Imprisoned without supporting proof, receiving sentence at the eleventh hour

definitions.text: Imprisoned without supporting proof, receiving sentence
definitions.meaning: read cryptically: in the nick (in jail) on account of time, the sentence handed down
at the last possible moment, just before it is too late

explanation.walkthrough: The NICK is British slang for prison and TIME for a jail sentence, so the phrase can be read as being locked up for a term.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means arriving or acting just before a deadline, exactly what the eleventh hour describes.

clue.text: Centre died in obscurity

indicators.note: the letter for died is placed in the word for obscurity

parts.note: mist causes obscurity, hiding things from view
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies and records

explanation.surface: A centre of activity passed away unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle or centre of something is its heart, a synonym in the phrase in the middle of.

clue.text: Russian novel died — see doctor at 5

parts.note: OB is short for Latin obiit, he or she died
LO is an old word meaning look or see
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A Russian story in which someone dies and a doctor is told to call at five.
explanation.definitionFit: Goncharov's novel about an idle landowner, whose title is the hero's surname, is a classic of Russian literature.

clue.text: Companion enters grain store, most of it in chaos

indicators.note: the companion goes into the shortened store, so one piece is placed within the other
only the larger part of the store is kept, its opening letters being dropped

parts.note: a granary is a building for storing grain
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A friend walks into a barn and finds most of it in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of it' drops the first two letters of the store, so only the larger part is kept before the companion goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of lawless disorder, a synonym for chaos.

clue.text: City street in comfort

indicators.note: the street abbreviation is put inside the word for comfort

parts.note: to cheer someone up is to comfort them

explanation.surface: A city street where people are at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a walled cathedral city in Cheshire, northwest England.

clue.text: Where NHS staff are making progress

definitions.meaning: nurses and doctors of the National Health Service work in hospital rooms for patients, so they are on duty there

explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; split as two words the answer says where its staff are found.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means forward or further ahead, which is what making progress implies.

clue.text: Laker's index — Laker employed one who went solo

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a new way, so these words are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, including the S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket statistic for Jim Laker, the spin bowler, set beside the man himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' rearranges all sixteen letters of LAKERSINDEXLAKER. The Scottish sailor was marooned alone on an island for over four years, inspiring Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailor survived alone on a Pacific island, so he went solo in the most extreme sense.

clue.text: Corruptly reduce one's chances of losing money?

definitions.text: Corruptly reduce one's chances of losing money?

parts.words: Corruptly reduce one's chances of losing money?
parts.note: literally, putting a lining in your pockets stops coins falling out; the idiom means enriching yourself dishonestly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to profit dishonestly, usually by taking bribes or misusing office.

clue.text: Model princess left with farewell that can be destructive

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives the letter T
Princess Ida is the heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera
a wave is a gesture of farewell

explanation.surface: A model princess leaves with a farewell that could cause harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea surge does great damage to coasts, so it is something that can be destructive.

clue.text: Francis, the writer, a man about town? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece is round the other, a containment signal
this reverses the order just stated, so the town goes round the man instead

parts.note: the Great Wen was Cobbett's name for London, so wen can stand for a town
HE is a male pronoun, standing for a man

explanation.surface: A journalist is asked if he is a man about town, and the answer is the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'a man about town' would put the man round the town; 'On the contrary' flips that. The Great Wen was a nickname for London.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Wheen is a British journalist and author, biographer of Karl Marx.

clue.text: Buggy, perhaps, used for film returned: put cat in it

indicators.note: the cat is to be put inside the reversed word, so one piece goes into the other
turned back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: CINE is the prefix for things used in filming, as in cine camera
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A buggy that was used in a film has come back, and someone is told to put the cat in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Buggy here means full of bugs, not a pram; the clue's surface pushes the pushchair reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to insects, and buggy can mean full of bugs, so it is an example.

clue.text: Trouble with rent that could be destructive

parts.note: rent as the past participle of rend means torn
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Problems with paying rent could be ruinous.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade reverses the clue's order: TORN comes first, then ADO; 'with' simply joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent twisting windstorm causes great damage, so it is something that could be destructive.

clue.text: Come to call with drug

parts.note: hi is a greeting you call out
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Visit and call in, bringing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for hurry or hasten, often as in hie thee hither, meaning come quickly.

clue.text: See 1
Depriving of complacency with exalted music for words

parts.note: raised high, so up
a setting is music composed to accompany a text

explanation.surface: Composing lofty music to words shakes a smug listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsetting someone disturbs their calm, so it deprives them of their self-satisfaction.

clue.text: Priest in the limelight repeatedly

indicators.note: the priest's name sits within the clue's words, so it is extracted from them

explanation.surface: A clergyman keeps being thrust into the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' because the name appears twice: across 'thE LImelight' and again in 'limELIght'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was the priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel, in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Is hesitantly returning what's owed — this is left

indicators.note: going back, so the first two pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
er is the sound of hesitation
something due is owed

explanation.surface: Someone stammers as they repay a debt, and this is what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the rest has gone is the leftover part, so this is left.

clue.text: Time for the Eastern sun

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East or Eastern
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Time for the sun to rise in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, a synonym for time as in the time of the Tudors.

clue.text: Source of wool for king and wood for spacecraft

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ash is a tree and its timber
Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station

explanation.surface: Sourcing wool for a king and timber for a spaceship.
explanation.definitionFit: The region gives its name to cashmere, the fine goat wool, so it is the source of that wool.

clue.text: Criminals? If so, I am in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A crook asks whether, if they are criminals, he is now in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Sicilian or American crime syndicate are criminals by definition.

clue.text: Explorer with a girl he deceived

indicators.note: the letters are led astray, so they are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An explorer and a girl he misled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan explorer who sailed to the Americas.

clue.text: A star turn in a doctor to be a maintainer of air purity

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the doctor abbreviation

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

indicators.note: a turn here is a change of order, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A celebrity performs a turn as a doctor who keeps the air clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A star turn' looks like a celebrity act, but splits into fodder and the anagram signal. A gas trap is a water-filled bend in a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas trap is a U-bend in a drain that holds water to block foul gases, so it keeps the air pure.

clue.text: Jersey etc under weight, according to Marxist writer

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits below another, so it comes after it

parts.note: grams are units of weight
Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

explanation.surface: A jersey and similar garments are underweight, says a Marxist author.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Gramsci was an Italian Marxist theorist whose Prison Notebooks are widely read.

clue.text: See 7
Drier for the 'ead?

parts.note: a dryer for the head is a hair dryer; said in Cockney, dropping the first letter as 'ead does, leaves a word for the element that dries things

explanation.definitionFit: Moving atmosphere dries things, as when washing is hung out, so it is a drier.

clue.text: Doom-laden alternative to oil as possible fuel

parts.note: fat is used instead of oil for cooking

indicators.note: a possible form of the word is one of its rearrangements

explanation.surface: An ominous choice of fat over oil as a fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fateful means having grave, often disastrous consequences, so it is laden with doom.

clue.text: A place for treatment where there's no dip

parts.note: a clinic is where patients are treated

explanation.surface: A clinic where nobody takes a dip.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is technical: an aclinic line on Earth is where a magnetic needle has no dip.
explanation.definitionFit: Aclinic describes the magnetic equator, where the compass needle shows no downward dip.

clue.text: Intelligence and energy are ineffective

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Brains and energy turn out to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no use is pointless or ineffective, the same idea in other words.

clue.text: Jones found in a single shot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: Someone called Jones is found with a single shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones was the 17th-century English architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo Jones was the English architect, so his forename can be clued by his surname alone.

clue.text: Set up something for women?

definitions.meaning: the Women's ... is a British organisation for women

explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute, the WI, is a British community organisation for women, famous for jam and Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute something is to establish it, and the WI is a well-known institute for women.

clue.text: A striking affair, not petit mal or rubella?

definitions.text: A striking affair, not petit mal or rubella?

parts.words: A striking affair, not petit mal or rubella?
parts.note: a nickname for industrial strikes as a national ailment, contrasted with petit mal (French name) and rubella (German measles)

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was a foreign nickname for Britain's habit of frequent strikes in the 1970s.
